question: What is a converter dolly?
choice_a: A device that measures air pressure in the trailer brake system
choice_b: A hydraulic lift used to raise a trailer's landing gear
choice_c: A type of kingpin used only on triple trailers
choice_d: A coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel used to couple a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig
explanation: The manual defines a converter dolly as a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Section 7.1 - Converter Dolly

topic: Coupling Doubles - Positioning the Converter Dolly
question: How do you release the brakes on a converter dolly that uses air tank brakes rather than spring brakes?
choice_a: By opening the dolly's air tank petcock
choice_b: By disconnecting the safety chains
choice_c: By pulling out the tractor protection valve
choice_d: By using the trailer hand valve
explanation: The manual states to release dolly brakes by opening the air tank petcock, or, if the dolly has spring brakes, use the dolly parking brake control.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.1 - Position Converter Dolly in Front of Second (Rear) Trailer

topic: Coupling Doubles - Positioning the Converter Dolly
question: According to the manual, when should you wheel the converter dolly into position by hand?
choice_a: Whenever the dolly has spring brakes
choice_b: If the distance to move it is not too great
choice_c: Only when the tractor's air supply is disconnected
choice_d: Only after the pintle hook has been locked
explanation: The manual says if the distance is not too great, wheel the dolly into position by hand so it is in line with the kingpin.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.1 - Position Converter Dolly in Front of Second (Rear) Trailer

topic: Coupling Doubles - Positioning the Converter Dolly
question: When using the tractor and first semitrailer to pick up a converter dolly, what must you do immediately after coupling the dolly to the first trailer?
choice_a: Open the shut-off valves at the rear of the second trailer
choice_b: Raise the landing gear of the second trailer completely
choice_c: Immediately connect the safety chains to the second trailer
choice_d: Lock the pintle hook and secure the dolly support in the raised position
explanation: After moving the dolly to the rear of the first semitrailer and coupling it, the manual instructs to lock the pintle hook and secure the dolly support in the raised position before pulling the dolly into position near the second trailer.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.1 - Position Converter Dolly in Front of Second (Rear) Trailer

topic: Coupling Doubles - Connecting to Front Trailer
question: What is the first step listed for connecting a converter dolly to the front trailer?
choice_a: Back the first semitrailer into position in front of the dolly tongue
choice_b: Lower the dolly landing gear completely
choice_c: Connect the air hoses to the front trailer
choice_d: Test the coupling by pulling against the kingpin
explanation: The manual lists backing the first semitrailer into position in front of the dolly tongue as the first step, followed by hooking the dolly to the front trailer and locking the pintle hook.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.1 - Connect Converter Dolly to Front Trailer

topic: Coupling Doubles - Connecting to Rear Trailer
question: Before backing a converter dolly under the rear trailer, the trailer height must be:
choice_a: At least six inches higher than the fifth wheel
choice_b: Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under
choice_c: It does not matter as long as the landing gear is down
choice_d: Exactly level with the top of the fifth wheel
explanation: The manual states trailer height must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.1 - Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

topic: Coupling Doubles - Connecting to Rear Trailer
question: While backing the converter dolly under the rear trailer, why should you raise the trailer's landing gear slightly off the ground?
choice_a: To prevent damage to the landing gear if the trailer moves
choice_b: To make the trailer height easier to measure
choice_c: Because the parking brakes cannot be applied otherwise
choice_d: To allow the safety chains to be connected
explanation: The manual instructs to raise the landing gear slightly off the ground to prevent damage if the trailer moves while the dolly is backed underneath.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.1 - Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

topic: Coupling Doubles - Connecting to Rear Trailer
question: After backing the dolly under the rear trailer, how do you test that the coupling is secure?
choice_a: Check the air pressure gauge in the cab
choice_b: Apply the trailer service brakes only
choice_c: Pull against the pin (kingpin) of the second semitrailer
choice_d: Drive the rig forward at highway speed
explanation: The manual directs the driver to test the coupling by pulling against the pin of the second semitrailer.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.1 - Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

topic: Coupling Doubles - Connecting to Rear Trailer
question: A proper visual check of a fifth-wheel coupling should confirm that:
choice_a: The landing gear is fully lowered
choice_b: There is no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel and the locking jaws are closed on the kingpin
choice_c: The dolly air tank petcock is open
choice_d: The safety chains are disconnected
explanation: The manual says to make a visual check of coupling: no space between upper and lower fifth wheel, and locking jaws closed on kingpin.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.1 - Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

topic: Coupling Doubles - Connecting to Rear Trailer
question: After coupling the converter dolly to the rear trailer and connecting safety chains, air hoses, and light cords, what should you do with the shut-off valves?
choice_a: Close the shut-off valves at the rear of the first trailer only
choice_b: Open every shut-off valve on the rig, including the rear of the last trailer
choice_c: Close the converter dolly air tank petcock and the shut-off valves at the rear of the second trailer, then open the shut-off valves at the rear of the first trailer (and dolly, if equipped)
choice_d: Leave all shut-off valves in whatever position they were found
explanation: The manual instructs to close the converter dolly air tank petcock and shut-off valves at the rear of the second trailer, then open the shut-off valves at the rear of the first trailer (and dolly, if so equipped).
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.1 - Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

topic: Coupling Doubles - Connecting to Rear Trailer
question: After raising the landing gear completely following coupling, what should you do to verify the trailer brake system is working?
choice_a: Immediately disconnect the safety chains to test them
choice_b: Charge the trailer brakes by pushing the "air supply" knob in, then check for air at the rear of the second trailer by opening the emergency line shut-off
choice_c: Chock the wheels of the tractor only
choice_d: Release the dolly parking brake and drive away
explanation: The manual instructs to charge trailer brakes (push "air supply" knob in) and check for air at the rear of the second trailer by opening the emergency line shut-off.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.1 - Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

topic: Coupling Doubles - Connecting to Rear Trailer
question: If you open the emergency line shut-off at the rear of the second trailer after coupling and there is no air pressure, what does this indicate?
choice_a: The trailer height was set correctly
choice_b: The dolly needs more grease
choice_c: Something is wrong and the brakes won't work
choice_d: The coupling was successful and everything is normal
explanation: The manual states that if air pressure isn't there when checking, something is wrong and the brakes won't work.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.1 - Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: Before uncoupling a set of twin trailers, where should you park the rig?
choice_a: In a straight line on firm, level ground
choice_b: On a slight downhill grade to help pull the dolly free
choice_c: Anywhere convenient, since parking brakes make ground condition irrelevant
choice_d: Only inside a maintenance bay
explanation: The manual instructs to park the rig in a straight line on firm level ground before uncoupling the rear trailer.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.2 - Uncouple Rear Trailer

question: When uncoupling the rear trailer, when should you chock the wheels of the second trailer?
choice_a: Only if the dolly has spring brakes
choice_b: Only if the coupling is on an incline
choice_c: Chocking is never needed if the parking brakes are set
choice_d: If it doesn't have spring brakes
explanation: The manual instructs to chock wheels of the second trailer if it doesn't have spring brakes.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.2 - Uncouple Rear Trailer

question: Why do you lower the landing gear of the second semitrailer slightly before pulling the dolly out during uncoupling?
choice_a: To engage the tractor protection valve
choice_b: To remove some weight from the dolly
choice_c: To raise the trailer height for measurement
choice_d: To disconnect the electrical cord automatically
explanation: The manual instructs to lower the landing gear of the second semitrailer enough to remove some weight from the dolly.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.2 - Uncouple Rear Trailer

question: After releasing the dolly brakes and the converter dolly fifth wheel latch, how do you separate the dolly from the rear trailer?
choice_a: Push the rear trailer backward away from the dolly
choice_b: Lift the dolly out using the landing gear crank
choice_c: Disconnect the kingpin with a wrench before moving anything
choice_d: Slowly pull the tractor, first semitrailer, and dolly forward to pull the dolly out from under the rear semitrailer
explanation: The manual instructs to slowly pull the tractor, first semitrailer, and dolly forward to pull the dolly out from under the rear semitrailer.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.2 - Uncouple Rear Trailer

question: Which of the following is a step in uncoupling the converter dolly itself, after the rear trailer has been separated?
choice_a: Immediately drive the tractor away at normal speed
choice_b: Open the shut-off valves at the rear of the last trailer
choice_c: Apply the converter gear spring brakes or chock the wheels, then release the pintle hook on the first semitrailer
choice_d: Reconnect the safety chains before disconnecting anything
explanation: The manual lists lowering the dolly landing gear, disconnecting safety chains, applying converter gear spring brakes or chocking wheels, releasing the pintle hook on the first semi-trailer, and slowly pulling clear of the dolly.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.2 - Uncouple Converter Dolly

question: Why does the manual warn never to unlock the pintle hook while the dolly is still under the rear trailer?
choice_a: It will damage the fifth wheel's glide plate
choice_b: It automatically drains all air from the tractor
choice_c: It will cause the tractor protection valve to fail
choice_d: The dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making it difficult to re-couple
explanation: The manual warns that never unlocking the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer risks the dolly tow bar flying up, possibly causing injury and making it very difficult to re-couple.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.2 - Uncouple Converter Dolly

question: When coupling a triple-trailer rig, what is the correct order of steps?
choice_a: Couple the third trailer first, then work forward to the tractor
choice_b: Couple all three trailers together before attaching the tractor
choice_c: Attach the dolly to the tractor before coupling any trailer
choice_d: Couple the tractor to the first trailer, then move the converter dolly into position and couple the first trailer to the second trailer using the doubles method
explanation: The manual instructs to couple the tractor to the first trailer using the tractor-semitrailer method, then move the converter dolly into position and couple the first trailer to the second trailer using the method for coupling doubles.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.3 - Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers

question: What is the correct procedure for uncoupling a triple-trailer rig?
choice_a: Release all pintle hooks simultaneously
choice_b: Uncouple the middle trailer first, then the third, then the first
choice_c: Uncouple the tractor from the first trailer before touching the rear trailers
choice_d: Uncouple the third trailer by pulling the dolly out and unhitching it using the doubles method, then uncouple the remainder as a double-bottom rig
explanation: The manual states to uncouple the third trailer by pulling the dolly out, then unhitching the dolly using the method for uncoupling doubles, and uncouple the remainder of the rig as you would any double-bottom rig.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.3 - Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers

question: For truck-trailer and tractor-trailer combinations not specifically described in the manual, what should a driver do?
choice_a: Avoid driving any combination not described in the manual
choice_b: Learn the correct coupling and uncoupling procedure according to the manufacturer's and/or owner's specifications
choice_c: Use the triples procedure as a universal default
choice_d: Always use the standard doubles coupling method regardless of vehicle type
explanation: The manual states there are too many combinations to cover, and the driver needs to learn the correct way to couple and uncouple the vehicle(s) according to the manufacturer and/or owner specifications.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.4 - Coupling and Uncoupling Other Combinations

question: What inspection procedure does the manual direct you to use as the basis for inspecting a doubles or triples combination vehicle?
choice_a: The pre-trip procedure used for straight trucks only
choice_b: The seven-step inspection procedure described in Section 2
choice_c: Only a visual check from the driver's seat
choice_d: A dolly-specific five-step checklist unique to Section 7
explanation: The manual states to use the seven-step inspection procedure described in Section 2 to inspect the combination vehicle, adding that there are more things to inspect than on a single vehicle.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Section 7.3 - Inspecting Doubles and Triples

question: When inspecting the lower fifth wheel on a doubles/triples combination, what should you check regarding the locking jaws?
choice_a: That the locking jaws are removed for easier coupling
choice_b: That the locking jaws match the color of the dolly
choice_c: That the locking jaws are closed around the shank of the kingpin, not the head
choice_d: That the locking jaws are painted a visible color
explanation: The manual specifies checking that the locking jaws are around the shank, not the head, of the kingpin.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.3.1 - Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

question: What should you check about the release arm on the lower fifth wheel during inspection?
choice_a: That it is disconnected to allow quick uncoupling
choice_b: That it has been removed for the trip
choice_c: That it is painted to match the tractor
choice_d: That it is properly seated and the safety latch/lock is engaged
explanation: The manual instructs to check that the release arm is properly seated and the safety latch/lock engaged, in addition to checking mounting, grease, and space between upper and lower fifth wheel.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.3.1 - Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

question: When inspecting the upper fifth wheel (mounted on the trailer), what two things should you check?
choice_a: That the landing gear crank is greased and the tires are inflated
choice_b: That the safety chains are the correct length
choice_c: That the trailer's shut-off valves are closed
choice_d: That the glide plate is securely mounted to the trailer frame and the kingpin is not damaged
explanation: The manual lists checking the upper fifth wheel for a glide plate securely mounted to the trailer frame and that the kingpin is not damaged.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.3.1 - Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

topic: Inspecting Doubles/Triples - Air and Electric Lines
question: When inspecting air and electric lines to the trailer, what should you verify about the air lines?
choice_a: They are properly connected to glad hands, show no air leaks, and are secured with enough slack for turns
choice_b: They are taped over to prevent moisture
choice_c: They are disconnected until just before departure
choice_d: They are routed underneath the fifth wheel
explanation: The manual states air-lines should be properly connected to glad hands, with no air leaks, properly secured with enough slack for turns, and all lines free from damage.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.3.1 - Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

question: What should you check regarding the sliding fifth wheel's locking pins during inspection?
choice_a: That only one locking pin is engaged
choice_b: That the locking pins are replaced with cotter pins
choice_c: That the locking pins have been removed for flexibility
choice_d: That all locking pins are present and locked in place
explanation: The manual states that for the sliding fifth wheel, all locking pins must be present and locked in place, and if air powered, there should be no air leaks.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.3.1 - Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

question: Why should you check that the sliding fifth wheel is not positioned too far forward?
choice_a: So the tractor frame won't hit the landing gear, or the cab won't hit the trailer, during turns
choice_b: So the air lines have enough slack
choice_c: So the trailer height matches the dolly exactly
choice_d: So the kingpin can be greased more easily
explanation: The manual instructs checking that the fifth wheel is not so far forward that the tractor frame will hit landing gear, or cab will hit the trailer, during turns.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.3.1 - Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

question: When inspecting the landing gear on a doubles/triples combination, what should you confirm?
choice_a: It is greased but left in the lowered position
choice_b: It is fully raised, has no missing or bent/damaged parts, and the crank handle is in place and secured
choice_c: It is lowered halfway to reduce strain on the fifth wheel
choice_d: It has been removed for combination vehicles
explanation: The manual states the landing gear should be fully raised, with no missing parts, not bent or otherwise damaged, and the crank handle in place and secured.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.3.1 - Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

question: According to the manual, what should the shut-off valve position be at the rear of the front trailer(s) versus the rear of the last trailer in a doubles/triples combination?
choice_a: Both should always be OPEN
choice_b: Rear of front trailers should be OPEN; rear of the last trailer should be CLOSED
choice_c: Rear of front trailers should be CLOSED; rear of the last trailer should be OPEN
choice_d: Both should always be CLOSED
explanation: The manual specifies that the shut-off valves at the rear of front trailers should be OPEN, while the shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer should be CLOSED.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.3.1 - Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

question: During inspection, what position should the converter dolly's air tank drain valve be in?
choice_a: OPEN
choice_b: Half-open to allow moisture to drain continuously
choice_c: It has no drain valve
choice_d: CLOSED
explanation: The manual lists the converter dolly air tank drain valve as CLOSED among the items to check.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.3.1 - Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

question: What should you verify about the pintle-eye and pintle hook during the walk-around inspection of a doubles/triples combination?
choice_a: That the pintle-eye of the dolly is in place in the pintle hook of the trailer(s) and that the pintle hook is latched
choice_b: That the pintle hook is lubricated with brake fluid
choice_c: That the pintle hook is left unlatched for quick release
choice_d: That the pintle-eye has been removed for triples
explanation: The manual instructs to be sure the pintle-eye of the dolly is in place in the pintle hook of the trailer(s), and to make sure the pintle hook is latched.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.3.2 - Additional Things to Check during a Walk-around Inspection

question: If a spare tire is carried on the converter dolly (converter gear), what must you make sure of during inspection?
choice_a: That it is mounted on the fifth wheel
choice_b: That it is secured
choice_c: That it is removed before coupling
choice_d: That it is inflated to double normal pressure
explanation: The manual states that if a spare tire is carried on the converter gear (dolly), make sure it's secured.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.3.2 - Additional Things to Check during a Walk-around Inspection

topic: Air Brake Checks - Air Flow to All Trailers
question: To check that air flows to all trailers, after building normal air pressure and pushing in the red "trailer air supply" knob, what do you do at the rear of the rig?
choice_a: Apply the trailer service brakes with the foot pedal only
choice_b: Immediately release the tractor parking brake
choice_c: Open the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer; you should hear air escaping, showing the system is charged
choice_d: Disconnect the electrical cord and check for sparks
explanation: The manual instructs going to the rear of the rig and opening the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer; hearing air escaping shows the entire system is charged.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.4.1 - Additional Air Brake Checks, Check That Air Flows to All Trailers

topic: Air Brake Checks - Air Flow to All Trailers
question: If you do NOT hear air escaping from both the emergency and service lines when checking air flow to all trailers, what should you do?
choice_a: Add more air to the dolly's spare tire
choice_b: Check that the shut-off valves on the trailer(s) and dolly(ies) are in the OPEN position
choice_c: Assume the system is fully charged and continue
choice_d: Replace the converter dolly immediately
explanation: The manual states that if you do NOT hear air escaping from both lines, check that the shut-off valves on the trailer(s) and dolly(ies) are in the OPEN position, since you must have air all the way to the back for all the brakes to work.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.4.1 - Additional Air Brake Checks, Check That Air Flows to All Trailers

topic: Air Brake Checks - Tractor Protection Valve
question: How do you test the tractor protection valve?
choice_a: Open the converter dolly air tank petcock while driving
choice_b: Charge the air brake system, shut off the engine, then step on and off the brake pedal several times to reduce tank air pressure and watch for the trailer air supply control to pop out
choice_c: Drive at highway speed and slam on the brakes
choice_d: Disconnect the trailer and check the tractor alone
explanation: The manual describes charging the trailer air brake system, shutting the engine off, and stepping on and off the brake pedal several times to reduce air pressure, watching for the trailer air supply control to pop out or move to emergency.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.4.1 - Additional Air Brake Checks, Test Tractor Protection Valve

topic: Air Brake Checks - Tractor Protection Valve
question: The trailer air supply control (tractor protection valve control) should pop out, or move from normal to emergency, when air pressure falls into what range, according to the manual?
choice_a: Usually within 60 to 80 psi
choice_b: Exactly 100 psi
choice_c: Usually within 20 to 45 psi
choice_d: Usually within 5 to 10 psi
explanation: The manual states the control should activate when air pressure falls into the pressure range specified by the manufacturer, usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.4.1 - Additional Air Brake Checks, Test Tractor Protection Valve

topic: Air Brake Checks - Tractor Protection Valve
question: What could happen if the tractor protection valve does not work properly?
choice_a: The trailer lights would fail to work
choice_b: The landing gear would lower unexpectedly
choice_c: An air hose or trailer brake leak could drain all the air from the tractor, causing emergency brakes to come on with possible loss of control
choice_d: The fifth wheel would automatically unlock
explanation: The manual warns that if the tractor protection valve doesn't work properly, an air hose or trailer brake leak could drain all the air from the tractor, causing the emergency brakes to come on, with possible loss of control.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.4.1 - Additional Air Brake Checks, Test Tractor Protection Valve

topic: Air Brake Checks - Trailer Emergency Brakes
question: How do you test the trailer emergency brakes?
choice_a: Apply the foot brake pedal only while parked
choice_b: Charge the trailer air brake system, check that the trailer rolls freely, then stop and pull out the trailer air supply control (or place it in the emergency position) and pull gently on the trailer with the tractor
choice_c: Disconnect the safety chains and observe the trailer
choice_d: Check the tire pressure on the trailer axles
explanation: The manual instructs charging the trailer air brake system, checking that the trailer rolls freely, then stopping and pulling out the trailer air supply control (or placing it in the emergency position), and pulling gently on the trailer to check the emergency brakes engage.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.4.1 - Additional Air Brake Checks, Test Trailer Emergency Brakes

topic: Air Brake Checks - Trailer Service Brakes
question: How do you test the trailer service brakes?
choice_a: Turn off the engine and listen for air leaks
choice_b: Only check the trailer brakes visually without moving the vehicle
choice_c: Check for normal air pressure, release the parking brakes, move the vehicle forward slowly, and apply the trailer brakes with the hand control (trolley valve); you should feel the brakes come on
choice_d: Apply the parking brake and check for a hissing sound
explanation: The manual instructs checking for normal air pressure, releasing the parking brakes, moving the vehicle forward slowly, and applying trailer brakes with the hand control (trolley valve); feeling the brakes come on confirms they are connected and working.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.4.1 - Additional Air Brake Checks, Test Trailer Service Brakes
